facts.topic: Q1: permission token types in cli-config.json
facts.detail: permissions.allow and permissions.deny are string arrays of exactly five token types: Shell(commandBase), Read(pathOrGlob), Write(pathOrGlob), WebFetch(domainOrPattern), Mcp(server:tool). Locations: ~/.cursor/cli-config.json (global) and <project>/.cursor/cli.json (project level, permissions only — all other CLI settings are global-only). Deny rules take precedence over allow rules.

Shell(commandBase) matches on the FIRST token of the command line and supports glob patterns plus an optional colon `command:args` syntax for finer control. Documented examples: Shell(ls), Shell(git) (allows any git subcommand), Shell(npm), Shell(curl:*) (curl with any arguments), Shell(rm) in deny. The docs' pattern-matching section says: 'Use command:args (e.g., curl:*) to match both command and arguments with globs'. A space-separated form like Shell(git *) is NOT documented anywhere — only the colon form.

Read(pathOrGlob) and Write(pathOrGlob) support glob patterns with **, *, and ? wildcards. Relative paths are scoped to the current workspace; absolute paths can target files outside the project. Examples: Read(src/**/*.ts), Read(**/*.md), Read(.env*), Read(/etc/passwd), Write(src/**), Write(package.json), Write(**/*.key), Write(**/.env*).

facts.topic: Q1: WebFetch and Mcp permission syntax
facts.detail: WebFetch(domainOrPattern): `*` matches all domains, `*.example.com` matches subdomains, `example.com` matches exact domain only; without an allowlist entry each fetch prompts. Mcp(server:tool): server name comes from mcp.json, `*` wildcards allowed on either side — Mcp(datadog:*), Mcp(*:search), Mcp(*:*).

cli-config.json optional field `approvalMode` (string) has exactly three documented values: "allowlist", "auto-review", "unrestricted". Auto-review runs allowlisted calls immediately, sandboxes other shell commands when possible, and sends the rest to a classifier (Claude 4.5 Haiku or GPT-5.4 Mini); Allowlist is deterministic with no classifier. Auto-review is additionally steered by a separate permissions.json with allow_instructions / block_instructions (plain-English policies).

facts.topic: Q1: sandbox config in cli-config.json — values NOT enumerated
facts.detail: cli-config.json documents `sandbox.mode` (string, 'Sandbox mode override') and `sandbox.networkAccess` (string, 'Network access setting for sandbox mode') but never enumerates their legal values; the /sandbox slash command configures them interactively. The separate editor-side ~/.cursor/sandbox.json or <ws>/.cursor/sandbox.json IS fully documented: `type`: "workspace_readwrite" (default) | "workspace_readonly" | "insecure_none"; `networkPolicy.default`: "allow" | "deny" (default deny) with allow/deny arrays (exact domain, *.wildcard, CIDR); plus additionalReadwritePaths, additionalReadonlyPaths, disableTmpWrite, enableSharedBuildCache.

facts.topic: Q2: no global env-var injection surface
facts.detail: The complete cli-config.json schema contains NO `env` block or any equivalent of Claude settings.json's "env" injection. Documented env surfaces are only: (a) mcp.json per-server `env` object and `envFile` (envFile STDIO-only; remote HTTP/SSE servers must use interpolation with shell-profile env vars instead), (b) `${env:NAME}` config interpolation resolved in mcp.json fields command, args, env, url, headers — plus ${userHome}, ${workspaceFolder}, ${workspaceFolderBasename}, ${pathSeparator}/${/}, (c) proxy vars the CLI reads from the shell environment (HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS), and (d) Cursor-injected read-only vars in sandboxed child processes (CURSOR_SANDBOX=seatbelt|native, CURSOR_ORIG_UID, CURSOR_ORIG_GID) — outbound only, not user-configurable.

facts.topic: Q3: subagent .md frontmatter — full documented field list
facts.detail: Exactly five fields, all optional: `name` (string, default derived from filename, lowercase+hyphens), `description` (string, shown in Task tool hints, drives automatic delegation), `model` (string, default `inherit`; or a specific model ID with optional bracket parameters like claude-opus-5[effort=high,context=300k] or composer-2.5[fast=false]), `readonly` (boolean, default false — restricts write permissions: no file edits, no state-changing shell commands), `is_background` (boolean, default false — runs without blocking the parent). `tools` and `color` are NOT documented fields.

facts.topic: Q3: subagent file locations and precedence
facts.detail: Project: .cursor/agents/, plus .claude/agents/ and .codex/agents/ for compatibility. User: ~/.cursor/agents/, ~/.claude/agents/, ~/.codex/agents/. Project subagents beat user subagents on name conflict; .cursor/ beats .claude/ and .codex/. Cursor also ships three built-in subagents (Explore, Bash, Browser) that need no configuration. Explicit invocation is via /name in the prompt.

facts.topic: Q4: rules file format — .mdc required, plain .md ignored
facts.detail: Project rules in .cursor/rules must use the .mdc extension. Verbatim: 'A plain .md file in .cursor/rules is ignored by the rules system because it has no frontmatter to specify description, globs, and alwaysApply. If you prefer plain markdown, use AGENTS.md instead.' .mdc frontmatter fields: description, globs (comma-separated patterns allowed), alwaysApply. Four application types: Always Apply, Apply Intelligently (description-based), Apply to Specific Files (globs), Apply Manually (@-mention).

facts.topic: Q4: user-level global rules — no documented ~/.cursor/rules/ directory or global file
facts.detail: Docs document NO ~/.cursor/rules/ directory and no single global rules file on disk. User Rules are global plain-text preferences defined in the app UI (Customize → Rules), apply across all projects, and are used by Agent (Chat) only — not Inline Edit or Tab. AGENTS.md is supported as plain markdown in the project root and nested subdirectories (nested files merge, more specific wins), but no ~/.cursor/AGENTS.md or other home-directory global file is documented. Precedence: Team Rules → Project Rules → User Rules.

facts.topic: Q5: Claude hooks compat — enablement and config locations
facts.detail: Requires enabling 'Third-party skills' in Cursor Settings → Rules, Skills, Subagents → 'Include third-party Plugins, Skills, and other configs' (feature must be enabled for the account). Claude hooks load from .claude/settings.local.json, .claude/settings.json, and ~/.claude/settings.json. Merge priority (highest→lowest): Enterprise hooks → Team hooks → .cursor/hooks.json (project) → ~/.cursor/hooks.json (user) → .claude/settings.local.json → .claude/settings.json → ~/.claude/settings.json. All matching hooks from every source run; higher-priority sources win on conflicting responses. Config files are watched and hot-reloaded.

facts.topic: Q5: Claude hooks compat — exact event mapping table
facts.detail: Auto-mapped (supported=Yes): PreToolUse→preToolUse, PostToolUse→postToolUse, Stop→stop, SubagentStop→subagentStop, SessionStart→sessionStart, SessionEnd→sessionEnd, PreCompact→preCompact, UserPromptSubmit→beforeSubmitPrompt. NOT supported: Notification, PermissionRequest. Tool-name mapping in matchers: Bash→Shell, Read→Read, Write→Write, Edit→Write, Grep→Grep, Task→Task; Glob, WebFetch, WebSearch have no mapping (unsupported). Supported features: command hooks, prompt hooks (type: prompt), nested hookSpecificOutput AND flat response formats, exit code 2 = block (other nonzero codes fail-open), regex tool matchers, timeout configuration.

facts.topic: Q5: Claude hooks compat — documented limitations
facts.detail: Native-Cursor-format-only features: the subagentStart hook (Claude only has SubagentStop), loop_limit configuration, and Team/Enterprise hook distribution via dashboard. Response mapping: permissionDecision→permission, permissionDecisionReason→user_message, updatedInput→updated_input; for Stop/SubagentStop, decision:"block"+reason is treated as Cursor's followup_message. Separately, cloud agents run command-based hooks only (no prompt hooks) and never run sessionStart, sessionEnd, beforeMCPExecution, afterMCPExecution, beforeTabFileRead, afterTabFileEdit, workspaceOpen. Docs also warn generically: 'Some behavior differences may exist due to different execution environments.'

facts.topic: Q6: custom commands — docs page removed, replaced by Skills
facts.detail: As of Aug 2026 there is no commands documentation page: /docs/agent/chat/commands and /docs/commands return 404 (the former redirects to /docs/skills in HTML form), and llms.txt lists no commands page (only cli/reference/slash-commands, which covers built-in CLI slash commands like /model, /sandbox — not custom .md commands). Cursor 2.4 ships a built-in /migrate-to-skills that converts 'both user-level and workspace-level commands' to skills with disable-model-invocation: true, preserving explicit /name invocation. The .cursor/commands/ directory still exists in the product (listed among writable .cursor subdirectories in the sandbox reference) but has no format documentation.

facts.topic: Q6: Skills (the documented successor) frontmatter and no argument substitution
facts.detail: SKILL.md frontmatter fields: name (required, must match parent folder), description (required), paths (optional glob scoping; legacy `globs` accepted as fallback), disable-model-invocation (optional bool — true makes it behave like a slash command, invoked only via /skill-name), metadata (optional arbitrary key-value map). Skills load from .cursor/skills/, .agents/skills/, ~/.cursor/skills/, nested project dirs, plus Claude/Codex compat dirs .claude/skills/, .codex/skills/, ~/.claude/skills/, ~/.codex/skills/. Optional dirs: scripts/, references/, assets/. NO $ARGUMENTS/$1-style argument substitution is documented anywhere for skills or commands.

facts.detail: Approval policy is set via `[ui] permission_mode` in config.toml (values: "always-approve", "auto", "ask", ...). Modes: `default` (ask), `acceptEdits`, `plan` (compat), `auto`, `dontAsk`, `bypassPermissions` (product name: always-approve; CLI `--always-approve` / `--yolo` / `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`; ACP `_meta.yoloMode: true`). Always-approve and auto are mutually exclusive (always-approve wins). Admins lock always-approve off with `[ui] disable_bypass_permissions_mode = true` in `~/.grok/requirements.toml` or `/etc/grok/requirements.toml` (legacy `[ui] yolo = false` also works). Claude-compatible `permissions.defaultMode` in `.claude/settings.json` is also honored.

Rules live in `[permission]` in `~/.grok/config.toml` (global) and `<project>/.grok/config.toml` (per-project, discovered at every level from repo root to cwd). Two forms: (1) structured `rules = [{ action = "allow|deny|ask", tool = "bash|read|edit|grep|mcp|webfetch|websearch", pattern = "git *" }]`; (2) compact string arrays `allow = [...]`, `deny = [...]`, `ask = [...]` using rule strings `Bash(git *)`, `Bash(git commit:*)`, `Read(src/**)`, `Edit(**/*.rs)`, `Grep`, `MCPTool(server__tool)`, `WebFetch(domain:example.com)`. CLI: repeatable `--allow`/`--deny`. Claude `.claude/settings.json` `permissions.allow/deny/ask` (incl. `mcp__server__tool` spelling) is read too; `permissions.additionalDirectories` is parsed but NOT supported. Evaluation is severity-based across all merged sources: deny > ask > allow, regardless of file or order. Managed sources: `/etc/grok/managed_config.toml`, `~/.grok/managed_config.toml`, root-owned `/etc/grok/requirements.toml`. Rules load once at session start.

Order for each tool call: 1) PreToolUse hooks (can deny; allow only declines to deny; hooks FAIL OPEN on crash/timeout), 2) permission rules (deny > ask > allow), 3) remembered per-project grants (opt-in via `[ui] remember_tool_approvals = true`; stored outside the repo, scoped to git repo root; dangerous commands `rm, chmod, chown, chgrp, chattr, pkill, kill, killall, git push` only honor exact-full-command grants), 4) built-in read-only auto-approvals (read_file, list_dir, grep, web_search, todo_write, and a fixed read-only shell list: ls/cat/git status/git diff/rg/kubectl get etc., checked per chain segment), 5) prompt policy from the mode. Bash chains are split on `&&`,`||`,`;`,`|`; deny/ask check every segment, allow checks only the whole string. Env-prefixes and wrappers (timeout, nice, ionice, chrt, stdbuf, env) are peeled for deny/ask, not for allow; sudo/xargs/nohup are not peeled. Read/Edit deny rules also apply to file paths shell commands touch, incl. inline `bash -c` scripts.

Sandbox is off by default; OS-level (Landlock/bubblewrap+seccomp on Linux, Seatbelt on macOS), applied to the whole process at startup, irreversible for the session, saved with the session (resume cannot change it). Selection: `--sandbox <profile>` > `GROK_SANDBOX` env > `[sandbox] profile` in config.toml > off. Built-in profiles: `off`, `workspace` (read everywhere; write CWD + ~/.grok/ + temp), `devbox`, `read-only`, `strict` (read CWD + system paths only). Child-network blocking is Linux-only (no-op on macOS). Custom profiles in `~/.grok/sandbox.toml` or `.grok/sandbox.toml` under `[profiles.<name>]` with fields: `extends` (string, one of workspace/devbox/read-only/strict, default workspace), `restrict_network` (bool), `read_only` (string[], literal dirs, globs skipped with warning), `read_write` (string[], literal dirs), `deny` (string[], paths or gitignore-style globs; kernel-enforced read+write/rename deny; on Linux requires bubblewrap, globs expanded only at launch; malformed globs = refuse to start). User-file profile beats identically-named project profile with a startup warning. Custom profiles fail closed (refuse to start) if unapplicable; built-ins warn and continue.

facts.topic: Q2: Subagent/agent definition locations and format
facts.detail: Agent definitions are Markdown files with YAML frontmatter (`---` delimited, parsed by serde_yaml; body after frontmatter = system prompt, appended per `promptMode`). Discovery (code: xai-grok-agent/src/discovery.rs): `.grok/agents/` and `.claude/agents/` walking cwd→repo root (project), then `~/.grok/agents/` (user), `~/.claude/agents/` (compat), `~/.grok/bundled/agents/` (lowest). Name-dedup: only PROJECT-level agents can shadow built-ins (`general-purpose`, `explore`, `plan`); a user-level `~/.grok/agents/explore.md` does NOT shadow built-in explore. Personas are separate: `.toml` files in `.grok/personas/` (project) > `~/.grok/personas/` (user) > bundled, or inline `[subagents.personas.<name>]` in config.toml (fields: instructions, instructions_file, description, inputs/outputs contracts, model, reasoning_effort, default_isolation). Roles: `.grok/roles/*.toml` or `[subagents.roles.<name>]` (description, default_capability_mode, model, prompt_file).

From `AgentDefinition` struct in crates/codegen/xai-grok-agent/src/config.rs (serde rename_all = camelCase; doc comment: 'parsed from .grok/agents/*.md'): required `name`, `description`; optional `promptMode` (extend|full, default extend), `capabilityMode` (read-only|read-write|execute|all), `permissionMode`, `skills` (list), `discoverSkills` (bool, default true), `inheritSkills` (bool, default true), `agentsMd` (bool, default true), `injectDefaultTools` (bool, default true), `tools` (string or list; allowlist, also carries Agent(type) spawn directives), `disallowedTools`, `effort`, `maxTurns` (>0), `isolation` (none|worktree), `background` (bool), `color`, `initialPrompt`, `mcpServers`, `mcpInheritance` (all | none | named:[...] | except:[...]), `hooks`, `memory`, `model`, `completionRequirement` ({tool, reminder, recovery{maxRetries, baseDelayMs, maxDelayMs}}), `toolOverrides`, `userMessageTemplate`, plus `toolConfig`/bash overrides ({timeoutSecs, outputByteLimit, cmdPrefix}). Plugin agents may NOT declare mcpServers, hooks, or permissionMode: bypassPermissions.

Yes — Grok has a top-level `[shell_environment_policy]` table in config.toml with the SAME name and shape as Codex's: `inherit = "all|core|none"` (default all), `ignore_default_excludes` (default true; when false drops *KEY*/*SECRET*/*TOKEN*), `exclude = [globs]`, `include_only = [globs]`, `set = { NAME = "value" }` (forces/injects values into tool subprocess env). Applies to the bash tool and terminals on macOS/Linux/Windows; the non-persistent backend also filters login-shell captures; persistent-shell .rc exports are replayed unfiltered. Note: this shapes TOOL SUBPROCESS env only, not the whole Grok process; the GROK_CONFIG overlay explicitly cannot use `set` to inject values (filter fields only). Other env surfaces: `[session] load_envrc = true` loads .envrc; per-hook `env` maps in hooks JSON; per-MCP-server `env = {...}`. No Claude-settings.json-style global `env` block is documented (Grok reads settings.json for permissions and hooks only).

Both are supported. (1) `$GROK_HOME/rules/` (default `~/.grok/rules/`) is always scanned; EVERY `*.md` file in it loads regardless of name, alphabetically — arbitrary fragments or a single file both work. `~/.claude/rules/` and `~/.cursor/rules/` load under compat toggles `[compat.claude] rules` / `[compat.cursor] rules`. (2) `~/.grok/AGENTS.md` also works: code in xai-grok-agent/src/prompt/agents_md.rs adds grok_home as a discovery root with scan_named_files=true (doc comment: 'Read Agents.md from ~/.grok/, git repo root, and session cwd'), so the recognized named files (`Agents.md`, `Claude.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `AGENT.md`, `AGENTS.md`) are discovered directly under `~/.grok/`. Home rules load first, then project files repo-root→cwd (deeper wins on conflict). Loaded in full, no truncation. `grok inspect` lists what loaded. Gitignored files are skipped in project discovery.

Verified in both docs and code. Docs (05-configuration.md, 'Goal mode and background workflows'): 'Project workflows are discovered from `<repo-root>/.grok/workflows/`; user workflows from `~/.grok/workflows/`.' Code (crates/codegen/xai-grok-shell/src/session/workflow/registry.rs): `user_workflow_dir() = grok_home().join("workflows")`; only `.rhai` extensions are listed; project dir requires folder trust, user dir does not. Invocation keys off the script's `meta.name` (keep filename aligned); precedence built-ins > project > user. Feature is on by default; disable via `[workflows] enabled = false` or `GROK_WORKFLOWS=0`. Bundled example: crates/codegen/xai-grok-shell/src/session/workflows/deep_research.rhai. Run state persists per-session under `<session-dir>/workflows/<run-id>/script.rhai` + `scripts/NNNN.rhai` revisions. Managed via `/workflow`, `/workflows` dashboard, `/deep-research`, and the `workflow` tool.

Experimental cross-session memory, disabled by default (enable: `GROK_MEMORY=1` or `[memory] enabled = true`; `GROK_MEMORY=0` force-disables). Storage is plain Markdown: `~/.grok/memory/MEMORY.md` (global), `~/.grok/memory/<project-slug>-<hash8>/MEMORY.md` (workspace; hash8 derived from origin remote org/repo, so clones and worktrees of the same repo SHARE one memory dir), `~/.grok/memory/<project-slug>-<hash8>/sessions/` (per-session logs). SQLite index (FTS5 + optional vec0 vectors) supports search; embedding model unset by default (full-text only). Commands: `/remember`, `/flush` (LLM summary), `/dream` (consolidation, auto-gated via [memory.dream]), `/memory` browser; model tools memory_search / memory_get; first-turn injection via [memory.initial_injection]. CLI: `grok memory clear [--workspace|--global|--all|--yes]`.

No dedicated export/import command exists (the only `grok memory` subcommand is `clear`). Migration is effectively supported because storage is plain Markdown you may edit or copy directly ('You can edit memory files directly under ~/.grok/memory/'; docs suggest `$EDITOR ~/.grok/memory/MEMORY.md`); a file watcher ([memory.watcher] enabled=true by default) reindexes created/modified/deleted files on the next memory search, so the SQLite index is derived state. Workspace dirs are keyed to the repo's origin remote (org/repo), so copied memory keeps matching the same repo on another machine as long as origin matches; path-keyed (non-git) workspaces would re-key if the path changes.

`~/.grok/config.toml` (main; only file where most sections load), `~/.grok/pager.toml` (appearance), `~/.grok/auth.json`, `~/.grok/sessions/`, `~/.grok/memory/`, `~/.grok/skills/`, `~/.grok/plugins/`, `~/.grok/agents/`, `~/.grok/hooks/` + `~/.grok/hooks-paths`, `~/.grok/sandbox.toml`, `~/.grok/rules/`, `~/.grok/workflows/`, `~/.grok/personas/`, `~/.grok/roles/`, `~/.grok/requirements.toml`, `~/.grok/managed_config.toml`. Project `.grok/`: config.toml (ONLY MCP servers, plugins, permission rules, and [mcp] max_output_bytes load project-scoped — other sections are user-global only), skills/, plugins/, agents/, hooks/, workflows/, personas/, roles/, sandbox.toml, lsp.json. GROK_HOME env relocates ~/.grok. Precedence: system requirements.toml/MDM > user requirements.toml > user config.toml > managed > GROK_CONFIG overlay (allowlisted soft settings only) > defaults; CLI flags > env vars > config files.

`[compat.claude]` cells (all default true): skills (~/.claude/skills/, <cwd>/.claude/skills/), rules (~/.claude/rules/, <dir>/.claude/rules/), agents (~/.claude/ named files + <dir>/.claude/CLAUDE*.md; plus `.claude/agents/` is scanned for agent .md definitions), mcps (~/.claude.json), hooks (~/.claude/settings.json), sessions (staged/inert). Grok reads `~/.claude/settings.json`, `settings.local.json`, and project equivalents for permissions rules and defaultMode; Ctrl+I imports Claude settings interactively. `[compat.codex]` is reserved/inert except sessions. Grok has no native config.local.toml — the documented personal-per-project rules file IS `.claude/settings.local.json`.

https://docs.x.ai/build returns HTTP 404 as of 2026-08-20; the repo's user-guide under crates/codegen/xai-grok-pager/docs/user-guide/ is the working primary source. The GitHub repo xai-org/grok-build exists (repo id 1300902838, description 'SpaceXAI's coding agent harness and TUI').

grokBuild.summary: All six gaps resolved from primary sources (repo user-guide docs + Rust source). Key findings: (1) approval policy is `[ui] permission_mode` plus `[permission]` allow/ask/deny rules (structured or compact string form) merged deny>ask>allow across ~/.grok/config.toml, project .grok/config.toml, .claude/settings.json, and managed layers; sandbox profiles (off/workspace/devbox/read-only/strict) select via `[sandbox] profile` and custom profiles live in `[profiles.<name>]` of ~/.grok/sandbox.toml or .grok/sandbox.toml with extends/restrict_network/read_only/read_write/deny. (2) Agents are .md files with camelCase YAML frontmatter in .grok/agents/ and ~/.grok/agents/ (full field list extracted from AgentDefinition in xai-grok-agent/src/config.rs); personas/roles are separate .toml files. (3) Grok has a Codex-identical `[shell_environment_policy]` table incl. `set` for injection (tool subprocesses only). (4) ~/.grok/rules/*.md accepts arbitrary fragments (single file fine) AND ~/.grok/AGENTS.md is a supported named-file path (confirmed in agents_md.rs). (5) ~/.grok/workflows/*.rhai is CONFIRMED as the user workflow surface in both docs and registry.rs code. (6) ~/.grok/memory/ is plain-Markdown cross-session memory with a derived SQLite index; no export command, but files are directly copyable/editable and the watcher reindexes.

facts.detail: HOOK_EVENTS in src/hooks/types.ts contains exactly 17 events: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, UserPromptSubmit, SessionStart, SessionEnd, Stop, StopFailure, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted, PreCompact, PostCompact, Notification, InstructionsLoaded, CwdChanged. Hook handlers are command-only (type: "command" with optional timeout). Output supports continue/stopReason/decision(approve|block)/reason/additionalContext.

Matcher is EXACT string equality only (matchesPattern in src/hooks/config.ts: matchValue === entry.matcher), no regex/glob. Match query per event: tool_name for PreToolUse/PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure, source for SessionStart, agent_type for Subagent*/Task*, trigger for Pre/PostCompact; other events have no matcher.

loadHooksConfig() reads ONLY loadUserSettings().hooks, i.e. ~/.grok/user-settings.json key `hooks`. Project-level .grok/settings.json hooks are intentionally excluded (comment: repo-committed file could execute arbitrary unsandboxed commands; hooks must be user-configured).

facts.topic: grok-cli MCP server storage — code wins over README
facts.detail: READS: loadMcpServers() returns loadUserSettings().mcp?.servers ?? [] — file ~/.grok/user-settings.json, key path `mcp.servers` (array of McpServerConfig {id,label,enabled,transport(stdio|http|sse),url,headers,command,args,env,cwd}). WRITES: saveMcpServers() calls saveUserSettings({mcp:{servers}}) which writeJson()s the SAME file USER_SETTINGS_PATH = ~/.grok/user-settings.json. The ProjectSettings interface for .grok/settings.json contains only model/sandboxMode/sandbox/lsp — no mcpServers field exists anywhere in code. README line ~186 claiming `.grok/settings.json` (`mcpServers`) is wrong on both the file AND the key. Call sites confirm: agent.ts buildMcpToolSet(loadMcpServers()) and app.tsx loadMcpServers()/saveMcpServers() are the only read/write paths.

facts.detail: The rules DSL supports THREE decisions, not just allow: `allow` (default; run outside sandbox without prompting), `prompt` (ask before each matching invocation), `forbidden` (block without prompting). No `deny`/`ask`/`confirm` keywords — those spellings are invalid. When multiple rules match, most restrictive wins: forbidden > prompt > allow. Source enum confirms: Decision::{Allow,Prompt,Forbidden}, parsed from strings "allow"/"prompt"/"forbidden". Mapping for auto-convert: Claude allow→allow, ask→prompt, deny→forbidden; precedence ordering is compatible (deny-most-restrictive-wins in both).

Patterns are argv PREFIX matches only. `pattern` is a list where each element is a literal string OR a union list of literals for that argv position (e.g. ["gh","pr",["view","list"]]). NO wildcards, NO regex, NO globs — source PatternToken::{Single,Alts} uses exact string equality per token, and the first token must be a fixed literal. `match`/`not_match` fields are validated inline examples, not patterns. So Claude Bash(cmd:*) prefix rules convert cleanly; any Claude rule needing mid-token wildcards, regex, or non-Bash tools (Read/Edit paths, WebFetch domains, MCP tool names) is NOT expressible in the rules DSL. Rules govern only commands run outside the sandbox; format is Starlark in .rules files under rules/ next to config layers (~/.codex/rules/, <repo>/.codex/rules/ when trusted); TUI allowlist additions write to ~/.codex/rules/default.rules; test with `codex execpolicy check`. Codex also splits bash -lc scripts into individual commands when they are plain words joined by &&/||/;/| (via tree-sitter) and applies rules per command, most restrictive wins; scripts with redirection/substitution/env vars/wildcards/control flow are evaluated as the single ["bash","-lc","<script>"] invocation.

Official Codex hooks docs exist (learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks.md). Exactly 11 events: PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, PreCompact, PostCompact, UserPromptSubmit, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, Stop, SessionStart, SessionEnd. There is NO PostToolUseFailure, StopFailure, Notification, TaskCreated/TaskCompleted, InstructionsLoaded, or CwdChanged event. Config lives in hooks.json or inline [hooks] in config.toml at ~/.codex/ and <repo>/.codex/ (project layer only when trusted); non-managed hooks require trust review via /hooks; matcher IS a regex string (unlike grok-cli's exact match). Only type:"command" handlers run today; "prompt" and "agent" handlers are parsed but skipped.

facts.topic: Codex hooks — unknown event name tolerance
facts.detail: The docs do NOT explicitly state unknown-event behavior; settled from source (main branch). hooks.json parses as HooksFile { description?, hooks: HookEventsToml } with #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] at the TOP level only: an unknown top-level key (e.g. putting "PreToolUse" at the root instead of under "hooks" — a likely Claude-porting mistake, covered by test hooks_file_rejects_events_outside_hooks_object) is a parse ERROR, which emits a startup warning and SKIPS THE ENTIRE FILE (load_hooks_json returns None on parse failure). But INSIDE the "hooks" object, HookEventsToml has NO deny_unknown_fields, so an unknown event name like "PostToolUseFailure" or "Notification" is SILENTLY IGNORED by serde — no error, no warning, and the recognized events in the same file still load. Same for inline TOML [hooks] tables.
facts.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/main/codex-rs/config/src/hook_config.rs (deny_unknown_fields on HooksFile only), https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/main/codex-rs/hooks/src/engine/discovery.rs (load_hooks_json warning+skip on parse error), https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/main/codex-rs/config/src/hooks_tests.rs (hooks_file_rejects_events_outside_hooks_object)

facts.topic: Codex PostToolUse fires on tool failure
facts.detail: Yes for shell: docs state explicitly "For Bash, it also runs after commands that exit with a non-zero status." Codex has no separate failure event — one PostToolUse covers success and failure, so grok-cli/Claude-style PostToolUseFailure handlers must be merged into Codex PostToolUse (the hook can inspect tool_response to distinguish). PostToolUse input includes tool_name, tool_use_id, tool_input, tool_response, turn_id; decision:"block" replaces the tool result with hook feedback (cannot undo side effects); exit code 2 + stderr also works; continue:false stops normal processing of the result. Hosted tools (e.g. WebSearch) never fire Pre/PostToolUse.
facts.source: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks.md#posttooluse ("PostToolUse runs after supported tools produce output... For Bash, it also runs after commands that exit with a non-zero status.")

facts.detail: timeout is in SECONDS (default 600; SessionEnd default 1, max 3) — Claude hooks timeout is also seconds but grok-cli differs. additionalContextLimit (~2500-token default) spills oversized output to disk. async:true runs hooks in background (cannot block). PreToolUse deny uses hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision:"deny" or legacy {decision:"block"}; permissionDecision:"ask" and legacy decision:"approve" are parsed but NOT supported yet (hook marked failed, tool call continues). PermissionRequest hooks can allow/deny pending approval prompts; any deny wins. Codex sets CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA env vars for plugin-hook compatibility. Feature toggle: [features] hooks = true/false in config.toml.

codeFacts.summary: All three tasks settled. (1) grok-cli: 17 hook events defined in src/hooks/types.ts (includes PostToolUseFailure, StopFailure, Notification, TaskCreated/Completed, InstructionsLoaded, CwdChanged); MCP servers are read AND written exclusively via ~/.grok/user-settings.json under `mcp.servers` (loadMcpServers/saveMcpServers in src/utils/settings.ts) — the README's `.grok/settings.json` `mcpServers` claim is wrong on both file and key, and hooks likewise load only from user-settings.json. (2) Codex rules DSL (Starlark .rules files, prefix_rule): three decisions — allow (default), prompt, forbidden — with most-restrictive-wins; patterns are argv prefixes of exact literals with optional per-position literal unions; no wildcards/regex/globs. So Claude allow/ask/deny all map (allow/prompt/forbidden) for Bash prefix rules, but only Bash-command rules convert; path/domain/MCP permission rules and mid-token wildcards do not. (3) Codex hooks docs are official and list 11 events with no failure-variant events; unknown event names inside the "hooks" object are silently ignored (serde: no deny_unknown_fields on HookEventsToml), while unknown TOP-level keys in hooks.json are a parse error that warns and skips the whole file; Codex PostToolUse explicitly fires for Bash commands with non-zero exit, so PostToolUseFailure handlers must merge into PostToolUse.
unresolved: Unknown-event tolerance is settled from main-branch source + serde semantics, not from docs or a live run; the docs page itself warns main-branch schemas may differ from the current release — a hands-on test (hooks.json with a bogus event name, check startup warnings and whether other hooks still fire) would confirm release behavior.

Whether Codex PostToolUse fires when an MCP tool call itself errors (protocol-level failure, not non-zero Bash exit) is not explicitly documented; docs only guarantee the Bash non-zero-exit case. Needs a hands-on test with a failing MCP tool.

Whether a hooks.json parse error (e.g. event at top level) blocks anything beyond skipping that file with a warning was read from load_hooks_json code; startup UX (how visibly the warning surfaces) untested.

grok-cli findings are from the main branch as of 2026-08-20; if the installed grok-cli version is older, the event list may be shorter — verify against the installed package's dist if pinning matters.
